claims.text: The two groups both record repeated `authentication failure` messages from the same SSH daemon, but they differ in source and timing pattern; the first group originates from a fully‑qualified hostname `n219076184117.netvigator.com` with failures clustered between 03:17 and 03:22 on June 22, while the second group comes from an IP address `60.30.224.116` and shows a burst of failures at 19:03 on June 30 followed by another cluster around 00:21 on July 1.

In both cases the target account is consistently `root`, indicating an attempt to gain privileged access, yet the hostname‑based source exhibits many more individual failure entries (over 30 timestamps) within a tight six‑minute window, whereas the IP‑based source shows only about 20 failures spread over two distinct night‑time intervals.

This concentration of rapid, repeated root login attempts from `n219076184117.netvigator.com` suggests an automated brute‑force or credential‑stuffing script targeting that host, making it the more anomalous source.

The root‑cause hypothesis is that a compromised botnet or malicious scanner is systematically trying default or weak credentials on SSH services reachable via `n219076184117.netvigator.com`, and the lack of any successful login or corrective action after these failures points to an ongoing, unmitigated attack.
